newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Hilton names ITT slate.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Hilton names ITT slate.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp Tuesday named 25 potential candidates for ITT Corp's board of directors if ITT rejects Hilton's $55 a share offer. The following is a copy of the company's statement.

BEVERLY HILLS, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Feb. 11, 1997--Hilton Hotels Corp. (NYSE:HLT) Tuesday provided notice to ITT Corp. (NYSE:ITT) of its intention to nominate candidates for ITT's board of directors at the company's next annual meeting of shareholders.
While ITT's 1997 annual meeting has not yet been scheduled, the annual meeting is regularly held in May.

Hilton reiterated its desire to meet with ITT management and the board of directors to discuss its $55-per-share acquisition offer, but said Tuesday's action was taken in case it becomes necessary to conduct a proxy contest to replace ITT's existing board in order to complete the proposed transaction.

The Hilton-proposed slate of nominees includes 25 individuals. Eleven of these individuals would be nominated to replace the existing 11-member ITT board. One or more of the other 14 would be nominated in the event ITT attempted to increase the size of its board, or if any of the first 11 individuals were unable for any reason to serve as an ITT director. Although Hilton believes any effort by ITT to increase the size of its board would not be legal, Hilton also said it is fully prepared to nominate the number of additional candidates necessary to replace the entire ITT board, regardless of its size.
The 25 individuals who are subject to nomination as ITT directors are listed below:
-- Daniel J. Altobello - Potomac, Md. - chairman of the board of ONEX Food Services Inc., and former chairman of the board, president and chief executive officer of Caterair International Corp.
-- George N. Aronoff - Cleveland, Ohio - partner, law firm of Benesch, Friedlander, Coplan & Aronoff.
Scott H. Bice - Pasadena, Calif. - Dean, University of Southern California Law School.
-- Barrie K. Brunet - Reno - former director and executive officer of Bally's Grand Inc.

-- Henry A. Collins - Bernardsville, N.J. - managing director and portfolio manager, Barrett Associates Inc., investment managers. Former director and senior vice president of Kidder Peabody, responsible for Equity Research and Institutional Equity Sales.
-- John Danhakl - Los Angeles - partner, Leonard Green & Partners, a private merchant banking firm.

-- Ernest E. East - Oro Valley, Ariz. - vice president, corporate secretary and general counsel, Artisoft Inc. and former vice president and general counsel of Elsinore Corp., Las Vegas; former vice president of Taj Mahal, Trump Plaza and Trump's Castle Casinos.
-- The Honorable James J. Florio - Piscataway, N.J. - partner, law firm of Florio & Perrucci, P.C.; former governor of the state of New Jersey.
-- Fred D. Gibson, Jr. - Las Vegas - chairman, president and chief executive officer of American Pacific Corp.
-- John E. Humphreville - Los Angeles - private investor.
-- Dianne Jett - Las Vegas - former president, Sprint-Central Telephone Co. of Nevada.
-- Robert L. Johander - Eden Prairie, Minn. - chairman and chief executive officer of ValueVision International Inc.
-- Russell D. Jones - Los Angeles - vice president, Sonnenblick-Goldman Co., real estate investment bankers.

-- Robert S. Kingsley - Far Hills, N.J. - private investor, former president and chief operating officer, HFS Gaming Corp. and former president and chief operating officer of Caesars World Resorts Inc.
-- Aubrey C. Lewis - Montclair, N.J. - former vice president of Woolworth Corp.
-- J. Kenneth Looloian - Carteret, N.J. - executive vice president, Di Giorgio Corp., a food distributor.
-- Rocco J. Marano - Chatham, N.J. - former president of Bell Communications Research Inc.
-- James F. McAnally, M.D. - Mendham, N.J. - director of nephrology at Elizabeth General Medical Center; director, Bally Total Fitness Holding Corp.
-- The Honorable Celeste Pinto McLain - Los Angeles - private attorney and arbitrator; member of the board of directors, National Railroad Passenger Corp. (Amtrak).
-- Justice Morris Pashman - Hackensack, N.J. - counsel to law firm of Pashman Stein P.C.; former Associate Justice on the Supreme Court of New Jersey; former mayor of Passaic, N.J.
-- Gilbert L. Shelton - Marshall, Va. - private investor.

-- Alan C. Snyder - Los Angeles - manager, Shinnecock Group, LLC, investment acquisitions; managing partner, Shinnecock Partners, private investors; former chief executive officer, Aurora National Life Assurance Co.; former president and chief operating officer, Executive Life Insurance Co.
-- Caroline L. Williams - New York - private investor; member of the board of directors, Argyle Television Inc., Swing-N-Slide Corp., DEVCAP Shared Return Trust. Former investment banker.
-- Robert H. Wolf - Beverly Hills, Calif. - president, Bob Wolf Co. Former chairman of the board and chief executive officer of Chiat/Day North America.
-- Warren C. Woo - Bethesda, Md. - president of corporate development, Snyder Communications Inc.

The following letter from Stephen F. Bollenbach, president and chief executive officer of Hilton Hotels Corp., was hand-delivered Tuesday to Rand V. Araskog, chairman and chief executive officer of ITT Corp.
February 11, 1997
Mr. Rand V. Araskog Chairman and Chief Executive Officer
ITT Corporation
1330 Avenue of the Americas New York, NY 10019-5490
Dear Mr. Araskog:
I am writing to express again our desire to meet with you and the management of ITT to discuss our proposal for a business combination of Hilton and ITT.

As you know, we believe this combination is a compelling one for both our companies and our respective shareholders. The initial response from shareholders and analysts has been overwhelmingly positive.

We also believe that the prompt consummation of our offer is in the best interests of both companies' shareholders, and an agreement now will allow us to achieve the best value for your shareholders. I am sure that you have read, as we have, the various press reports speculating on defensive mechanisms you might employ to keep our offer from your shareholders.

Of course, we have no knowledge of the accuracy of these reports, and we assume that you will not take actions to frustrate the wishes of your shareholders or to diminish the value of their equity. Let me reiterate, however, our commitments to making this combination a reality.

We do not intend to be deterred from pursuing our offer by any actions that you may choose to take. But, to the extent your actions reduce the value of the combination to us, we would, of course, be required to review the per share price that we would be able to pay and, if necessary, adjust the terms of our offer. We hope that upon your review of our offer, you and your Board will agree that this combination is in the best interests of ITT and your shareholders. We stand ready to meet with you at any time and to answer any questions you or your directors may have. We look forward to hearing from you.
Sincerely, Stephen F. Bollenbach
